scores.evidence: Keyword search catches error codes, button labels and feature names. Vector (meaning-based) search catches rephrasings
scores.rationale: Technically sound on hybrid retrieval, RRF, rerank, citation validation, pgvector; minor issue: a DPA guaranteeing no storage is overstated (abuse-monitoring retention), and streaming citation stripping vs post-hoc commitment check tension is not addressed.

scores.evidence: Label about 200 recent tickets as *answerable from current docs*, *needs account data or an action*, or *missing from the docs*.
scores.rationale: Precisely fits the request, resolves ambiguities with stated assumptions, has coverage audit, build-vs-buy, and explicit v1 exclusions with reasons.

scores.evidence: Hand off immediately when the user asks or the topic is sensitive
scores.rationale: Consistent pipeline with clear responsibilities; minor loose ends, e.g. commitment check after streaming has already shown text, and visibility filter vs. unauthenticated users is loose.

scores.evidence: Run the tests automatically on every change to prompts, models, chunking or embeddings, and block changes that make scores worse.
scores.rationale: Tests early (week 1), retrieval scored separately, LLM grader calibrated to human labels, shadow agent-assist phase, A/B control, weekly production review; thresholds labeled starting targets.

scores.evidence: 100–5,000 articles on a help-center platform with an API (Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk…) or Markdown files in git.
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit and questions say what would change the plan, but sensitivity is only partly explained and some numbers (most articles under 2k) are unqualified.

scores.evidence: The nightly check also **removes** archived or unpublished articles. Old articles left in the index lead to confident wrong answers.
scores.rationale: Covers stale content, leaks, injection via forum posts, commitments, hallucinated citations, abuse and frustration loops, but lacks webhook-failure detection and explicit partial-failure/outage handling of LLM or vendor.

scores.evidence: Keep prompts in version control. For every conversation turn, log the rewritten query, the retrieved IDs and scores
scores.rationale: Logging, tracing, eval gating and review cadence exist, but no concrete deployment, rollback, index re-embedding migration, alerting, or incident ownership.

scores.evidence: each message uses about 5–10k input tokens and about 300 output tokens. That's a few cents per conversation
scores.rationale: Identifies token cost, caching, model tiering, spending caps and build-vs-buy, but the estimate is thin, lacks per-conversation basis and scaling, and omits engineering and vendor costs.

scores.evidence: Orchestration | Your own thin code (easiest to debug) | LlamaIndex, LangGraph, Haystack
scores.rationale: Avoids heavy frameworks, uses Postgres rather than separate vector DB, swap-friendly stack, build-vs-buy; but embedding model/chunk ID scheme lock-in and re-index migration are not explicitly discussed.

scores.evidence: Use a fixed pipeline in v1: always retrieve, then answer. It's predictable, cheap and easy to test.
scores.rationale: Simple baseline with escalation path (contextual retrieval, agentic only if tests fail), vision deferred, forum excluded; a router and rewriter plus rerank are modestly extra but justified.

scores.evidence: Right article in the top 5 for ≥ 90% of answerable questions
scores.rationale: Phased plan with checkable exit criteria and sensible dependency ordering (test set first, shadow mode before beta); some details like adaptation on failure are only partly given.

checklist.evidence: Sync on publish events plus a nightly full check. ... The nightly check also removes archived or unpublished articles.
Split articles at H2/H3 headings ... Never split a numbered procedure or a table. ... store its ID, URL, section anchors, category, labels, locale
Build a test set of 200–300 cases from real tickets ... Run the tests automatically on every change to prompts, models, chunking or embeddings
Answer only from the provided docs. If they don't cover the question, say so plainly and offer a human.
The ticket includes the transcript, a two-line summary, what the user wanted, the articles shown and the user's plan
Leave community-forum posts out of v1. ... Rules 1–2 and the final check cover that.
Index only public articles, or store the permissions and filter on them.
Mask emails, phone numbers and card numbers before anything is logged ... Set how long transcripts are kept (e.g. 30–90 days).
Version 1 answers questions from the docs only. It can't look up or change customer accounts.
Each week, review about 50 random conversations plus every thumbs-down ... Missing-docs report
That's a few cents per conversation with a mid-size model, and less with prompt caching.

traps.evidence: Never fill gaps from general knowledge, especially prices, limits, timelines or policies.
Index only public articles, or store the permissions and filter on them.
Sync on publish events plus a nightly full check.
block changes that make scores worse
Use a fixed pipeline in v1: always retrieve, then answer.

note: Strong, well-scoped docs-only RAG plan with early evaluation and shadow rollout; weaker on operations/rollback, cost basis, and authenticated entitlement filtering.
